s.d: an edict of the Russian tsar
An authoritative proclamation; an edict, especially decreed by a Russian czar or later ruler.
x: Many estates peopled with crown peasants have been, according to an ukase of Peter the Great, ceded to particular individuals on condition of establishing manufactories […]
An Ukase, it appears, has been issued by the Emperor Alexander, to facilitate the introduction of calimancoes and other Norwich goods into his Empire.

s.d: (figuratively) Any absolutist order or arrogant proclamation
x: I knew a stunned plunge of disappointment and a bitter anger. What right had he to issue such an arbitrary ukase?

uke.e: From Japanese 受け (uke), the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 受(う)ける (ukeru, “to receive, to get”).

s.d: a small guitar having four strings
The training partner against whom tori performs a move.
(slang) A passive or submissive male fictional character in a same-sex relationship; a bottom.
x: Yaoi uke in fanfics often bear the brunt of stereotypical "negative female characteristics" such as passivity, helplessness, and masochism.
You'd rather have Sebas be an uke?

ukulele.e: Borrowed from Hawaiian ʻukulele, from ʻuku (“flea”) + lele (“jump, jumping”).
